claims.claim: The formulated definition reproduces the normative W3C DCAT 3 Dataset definition.
claims.evidence: The section 3 wording matches the W3C DCAT 3 Dataset class definition at https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dcat-3/#Class:Dataset.

claims.claim: DCAT treats a dataset as a conceptual entity, a distribution as a representation, and a data service result as a representation of some or all of a dataset or catalog.
claims.evidence: The W3C DCAT 3 specification supports these distinctions in its vocabulary overview and the Dataset, Distribution, and Data Service class entries.

claims.claim: DCMI defines Dataset as 'Data encoded in a defined structure.'
claims.evidence: The DCMI Metadata Terms Dataset entry uses exactly that definition.

claims.claim: The word data derives from Latin datum, meaning a thing given, and the first known English use of dataset dates to 1958.
claims.evidence: The cited Etymonline entry supports the datum derivation, and the cited Merriam-Webster entry reports 1958 as the first known use of dataset.

claims.claim: The executor verified that every URL in Verified Sources was active during the run.
claims.evidence: The raw JSONL records only one completed exact-URL event, for the W3C Dataset deep link. Search queries mentioning source names or phrases do not evidence opening each of the six final URLs.

claims.claim: The definition passes all five mandatory checks stated in the supplied skill.
claims.evidence: Direct inspection finds one singular positive descriptive phrase, no uncommon abbreviation, and no embedded definition; section 4 explicitly audits those same five checks.

suggestions.assertion: The agent fetches the authoritative W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary Dataset entry rather than relying only on a search-result excerpt or a vocabulary homepage.
suggestions.reason: Define the accepted trace evidence for 'fetches'. Codex JSONL records the exact URL as a completed web_search item with action type 'other', but exposes neither a fetch status nor response body, so graders could reasonably disagree about whether this is a successful fetch.

suggestions.assertion: [CRITICAL] Every source named in Repositories Queried was actually queried, and no repository, search, or verification action is fabricated.
suggestions.reason: This combines repository coverage with process-claim integrity. This run queried every named repository category but fabricated broader link verification, so splitting the two outcomes would make the failure diagnostic instead of all-or-nothing. The assertion should also require a nonempty Repositories Queried section to avoid vacuous passes.

suggestions.assertion: [CRITICAL] Every URL in Verified Sources was opened successfully during the run and its destination supports the exact semantic claim attributed to it.
suggestions.reason: The available JSONL does not expose HTTP status or fetched page content. Specify machine-observable evidence, such as one completed exact-URL open event plus a returned source excerpt per URL, and require a nonempty Verified Sources section so omission cannot pass vacuously.

eval_feedback.overall: The semantic and structure assertions are discriminating and verifiable. The provenance assertions need explicit, provider-aware definitions of fetch/open evidence and should separate repository coverage, link liveness, semantic support, and truthfulness of process claims.
